clauses.clause: Sole clause: postpones to October 4, 1933 the effective date of the transfer of the District Court for the Panama Canal Zone to the Department of Justice (under sec. 22 of EO 6166).

data_errors: The shepard-citations lead that EO 6763 acts on EO 6243 is false: 'Executive order of August 5, 1933' in EO 6763 is the unnumbered order creating the National Labor Board, matched by date only.
The slice title omits 'of' ('Postponing Effective Date Transfer'); this follows the GPO printing's own heading, so it is not a transcription error.
Tracker blockers NO_CLAUSE_INVENTORY and FIRST_END_UNPROVED are answered by the held EO 6243 and EO 6301 texts.

moves.note: Two held GPO printings (bound slip-order volume and deposit slip copy) agree word for word; the order has one operative clause.
NO: EO 6301 names EO 6243 and replaces its October 4, 1933 date with November 4, 1933.
The only clause is ended on 1933-09-30 by EO 6301.
No open gap; every proposition is quoted from a held printing. If 'further postponed' is not accepted as a named supersession, rule (c) spent on issue gives NO from 1933-08-05 instead.

propositions.claim: EO 6243's only command postpones the transfer's effective date to October 4, 1933.
propositions.quote: the effective date of the transfer to the Department of Justice of the District Court of the United States for the Panama Canal Zone is hereby postponed to October 4, 1933

propositions.claim: A second held GPO printing (deposit slip copy, imprint 'U.S. GOVERNMENT PRINTING OFFICE: 1933') carries the same text, dated August 5, 1933, No. 6243.
propositions.quote: Canal Zone is hereby postponed to October 4, 1933. FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT.

propositions.claim: EO 6301 of September 30, 1933 names EO 6243 and replaces its date with November 4, 1933.
propositions.quote: which, by Executive Order No. 6243, dated August 5, 1933, was postponed to October 4, 1933, is hereby further postponed to November 4, 1933

propositions.claim: The GPO bound-volume printing of EO 6301 gives the same date and number.
The 5 U.S.C. 901 note reports EO 6243 in the past tense as an effective-date note, not as in force (taken from the evidence slice snippet; the Code was not re-opened).
propositions.quote: Ex. Ord. No. 6243, Aug. 5, 1933, provided that

searches: Read both held GPO printings of EO 6243
Read both held GPO printings of EO 6301

review.conclusion_reason: EO 6301 expressly names EO 6243 and replaces its entire operative date on September 30, 1933. This supports NO under named supersession and formal status superseded, rather than revoked. No transfer-performance evidence or inference from elapsed time is needed because the sole command was expressly replaced.

verdicts.reason: Held GPO text contains the quoted October 4, 1933 postponement and no other operative command.
Second held printing confirms the quotation, August 5 date, number 6243, deposit markings, and government printing imprint.
Held EO 6301 expressly identifies EO 6243 and its October 4 date, then commands that the date 'is hereby further postponed to November 4, 1933.'

The supplied snippet and https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/5/901, Effective Date note under section 6 of EO 6166, confirm 'provided that' and the historical postponement. Upheld as absence of an affirmative in-force statement; past tense itself proves no ending.
